claim: HA cartilage exhibited severe damage compared with OA cartilage
source: Consistent with previous reports, the HA cartilage exhibited severe damage and significant hemosiderin deposition, compared with that of OA (Figure 1A).

claim: HA cartilage showed significant hemosiderin deposition compared with OA cartilage
source: Consistent with previous reports, the HA cartilage exhibited severe damage and significant hemosiderin deposition, compared with that of OA (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by visual evidence in Figure 1A with black arrow indicating hemorrhagic ferruginous deposits

claim: MRI analysis revealed subchondral bone loss in HA patients

claim: ABH staining detected substantial sulfated glycosaminoglycan (sGAG) depletion in HA cartilages

claim: HA cartilages showed prominent decrease in cartilage matrix protein COL2A1 compared to OA

claim: HA cartilages showed increase in expression of MMP13 compared to OA

claim: MMP13 is the primary enzyme responsible for cartilage degeneration
source: As expected, comparing to OA, HA cartilages showed prominent decrease in cartilage matrix protein COL2A1 and increase in expression of MMP13, the primary enzymes responsible for cartilage degeneration (Figure 1E, F).

claim: Obvious increase in DNMT1 protein levels was detected in HA cartilages compared to OA

claim: Obvious increase in DNMT3A protein levels was detected in HA cartilages compared to OA
source: Additionally, obvious increase in DNMT1 and DNMT3A protein levels was also detected in HA cartilages (Figure 1G, H), whereas no significant changes were found in DNMT3B (Figure 1-Figure supplement 1A, B).

claim: No significant changes were found in DNMT3B protein levels between HA and OA cartilages

claim: Global DNA methylation levels exhibited systematic differences between HA and OA

claim: 69.95% of DMRs were hypermethylated in HA compared to OA

claim: 30.05% of DMRs were hypomethylated in HA compared to OA

claim: 93.49% of DMRs were located in gene promoters, 5'-UTRs, 3'-UTRs, and exons

claim: 6.51% of DMRs overlapped intergenic regions
